Title: Heft
Author: Liz Moore
Why I recommend it: A man ashamed to be seen by anyone has shut the world out for ten years, and one phone call forces him to choose between staying hidden and letting someone in. Two people society would write off as losers each fight their own inner battle. Reading about them is deeply moving, because anyone who has ever struggled will understand.

Title: The Midnight Library
Author: Matt Haig
Why I recommend it: If you could undo every regret and live every other version of your life, would you still find one worth staying for? This book plays with the "what if" that can haunt us: what if we had decided differently and lived another life? The book shows that every life is unique and none is perfect.

Title: Long Bright River
Author: Liz Moore
Why I recommend it: A Philadelphia cop hunting a killer in her own neighborhood fears that the next victim could be her sister, who has disappeared into the city's drug scene. If you've ever watched a documentary about the drug scene in Kensington, Philadelphia, this book plays like a movie in your head. It's hard to put down.

Title: Real Americans
Author: Rachel Khong
Why I recommend it: How much of who we become is chosen by us, and how much is decided by our parents' ambitions, our genes and plain luck? Through three generations, this book explores class, nationality and how immigrants always live between two worlds. It's unexpected and deep without ever feeling preachy.

Title: Vom Mut, frei zu sein
Author: Marie Luise Ritter
Why I recommend it: You know the life you want, but the fear of what others will think keeps you from living it. The chapter on having children stayed with me: asked "Do you want to be a mum?", the answer might be no, but asked "Do you want to be a dad?", it would likely be yes. That's very telling.

Title: Tiny Experiments
Author: Anne-Laure Le Cunff
Why I recommend it: You've been told to chase big goals, but what if curiosity gets you further than ambition ever did? This is the only self-help book that has truly changed something for me. Instead of chasing linear goals, you run experiments and collect data points about your direction. That takes so much pressure off, and I now experiment regularly, which makes me happy.

Title: Atomic Habits
Author: James Clear
Why I recommend it: Willpower always runs out, so how do you change your life when motivation fades? This book is super powerful in combination with Tiny Experiments. Learning what you need, and creating habits around it, is everything you need for a happy and fulfilled life.
